chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hajjaj al-Khashshab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman who bequeathed to me wealth to be spent in the way of Allah, so it was said to her, 'It will be used for Hajj,' but she said, 'Spend it in the way of Allah.' They said to her, 'Shall we give it to the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?' She said, 'Spend it in the way of Allah.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Spend it in the way of Allah as she commanded.'

I said, 'Instruct me on how to spend it.' He said, 'Spend it as she commanded you. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says, "So if one alters the bequest after hearing it, then the sin is only upon those who alter it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing." Do you think if she commanded you to give it to a Jew, would you give it to a Christian?'

He said, So I waited for three years after that, then I entered upon him and said to him what I had said to him the first time. He paused for a moment, then said, 'Bring it.' I said, 'To whom shall I give it?' He said, 'Isa Shalaqan.'

key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Way of Allah (a general term for charity/good deeds, contextually specific here)
key_terms.عِيسَى شَلَقَانَ: Isa Shalaqan (a specific individual named as recipient)

ai.seo_question: How should a bequest designated as 'in the way of Allah' be executed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the Shia principle of strict adherence to the testator’s specific intent (*al-irada*) when executing bequests, cautioning against the executor’s subjective substitution of meaning for 'in the way of Allah' (*fi sabil Allah*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the analogy of changing a specific recipient (Jew to Christian) to illustrate that altering the designated beneficiary violates the divine command, a principle rooted in Quran 2:181 regarding those who alter bequests. The narrative concludes with the Imam’s eventual clarification that 'in the way of Allah' referred to a specific individual, Isa Shalaqan, highlighting the importance of precise execution in Islamic inheritance law.
